---
title: "Code used in class"
---

This folder holds the code examples, demonstrations and simulators used in lectures and labs. Many come from the textbook's [ostep-code](https://github.com/remzi-arpacidusseau/ostep-code) and [ostep-homework](https://github.com/remzi-arpacidusseau/ostep-homework) repositories. Browse the files on [GitHub](https://github.com/nipunbatra/os2018/tree/master/code).

## Contents

### Processes

- **Process API**: `fork_demo_*.c`, `exec_demo_*.c`, `wait_demo_*.c`
- **Process creation**: [`p1.c`](p1.c), [`p2.c`](p2.c), [`p3.c`](p3.c), [`p4.c`](p4.c)
- **Hello world programs**: [`hello.c`](hello.c), [`hello_world.c`](hello_world.c), [`hello_assembly.c`](hello_assembly.c)

### CPU scheduling

- **Scheduling simulator**: [`scheduler.py`](scheduler.py), [`cpu-virtual.py`](cpu-virtual.py)
- **MLFQ**: [`mlfq.py`](mlfq.py)
- **Lottery scheduling**: [`cpu-sched-lottery/lottery.c`](cpu-sched-lottery/lottery.c)

### Memory

- **Memory examples**: [`mem.c`](mem.c), [`mem2.c`](mem2.c), [`mem3.c`](mem3.c)
- **Address translation**: [`memory-address.c`](memory-address.c)
- **Virtual memory**: [`vm-intro/va.c`](vm-intro/va.c)
- **Memory simulation**: [`relocation.py`](relocation.py)

### Threads and concurrency

- **Thread examples**: [`hello_thread.c`](hello_thread.c), [`sum_thread.c`](sum_thread.c)
- **Thread API**: `threads-intro/`
- **Synchronisation**: code in the [lab folders](https://github.com/nipunbatra/os2018/tree/master/labs)

### I/O and system calls

- **I/O examples**: [`io.c`](io.c)
- **System call tracing**: `trace-io.*`

### Python simulators

- **CPU scheduling**: [`scheduler.py`](scheduler.py)
- **Memory management**: [`relocation.py`](relocation.py), [`x86.py`](x86.py)
- **Process execution**: [`process-run.py`](process-run.py)

### Assembly

- **Assembly code**: [`hello_world.s`](hello_world.s), [`loop.s`](loop.s), [`simple-race.s`](simple-race.s)
- **Threading**: [`looping-race-nolock.s`](looping-race-nolock.s)

## How to use

1. **Compilation**: Most C programs can be compiled with `gcc filename.c -o filename`
2. **Python scripts**: Run with `python3 script.py`
3. **Makefiles**: Use `make` in directories that contain Makefiles
4. **Threading**: Compile with `-pthread` flag for threading examples

## Common headers

- `common.h`: Shared definitions and includes
- `common_threads.h`: Threading-specific includes

## Subfolders

Subfolders from the textbook's code:
- `intro/`: Introduction examples
- `cpu-api/`: Process API exercises
- `threads-intro/`: Threading introduction
- `vm-intro/`: Virtual memory introduction
